name: ticker-strip-3840
story: A full-width news ticker - amber category flag, headline, clock - drawn on a 3840x120 Figma frame and exported as SVG with the id attribute included and text left live.
idioms: viewBox="0 0 3840 120" - a 32:1 strip, far wider than the 16:9 frame
no XML declaration at all (Figma writes none)
the frame wrapped in <g clip-path="url(#clip0_18_204)"> with the matching <clipPath> in <defs>
layer names written verbatim into id, spaces and all (id="News Ticker")
uppercase hex fills plus the literal fill="white"
every <text> carries xml:space="preserve" style="white-space: pre", typography as attributes, content in one positioned <tspan> with a fractional y
omitted x/y on rects that sit at 0, and completely flat (unindented) output
whyThisMatters: A placement rule that assumes an artboard is roughly frame-shaped either letterboxes this strip into a sliver or stretches it to 16:9; and a single-<tspan> Figma text must bind as ONE field, not be mistaken for a multi-line block, so a ticker headline stays one operator line. (Size corrected 2026-08-28: docs/SVG_AUTHORING.md §2 says artwork larger than the frame scales DOWN to it, vector, nothing lost - so a 3840x120 strip is reported at its fitted 1920x60 design size.)
